author: daniellehrner
content: Looks like that is an issue with the shadow fork. The shadow fork is around 2,500 blocks behind real Sepolia. Before the Glamsterdam hardfork Besu connects to regular Sepolia nodes, which are not part of the shadow fork, and those report that their head is those 2,500 blocks ahead. Because of that Besu thinks it needs to sync and during sync disables the tx pool. That explains the empty blocks. Once we fork off to Glamsterdam on the shadow fork we disconnect the regular Sepolia peers and only get the ones from the shadow fork. At this point the head of our peers and Besu is the same and we enable the tx pool again.

author: daniellehrner
content: We need to check how to do that differently, even though that is only shadow fork specific and does not happen on real networks
